📋 Executive Summary

The Production Batch module is a masterclass in robust application design, built upon three core architectural pillars:

⚙️

Strict State Machine

Meticulously separates the non-financial DRAFT phase from the irreversible IN_PROGRESS execution phase, ensuring data integrity.

🎯

Service-Layer Orchestrator

"Thin view, thick service" pattern. Business logic centralized in batch_service.py, making it highly auditable and testable.

🔄

Symbiotic Architecture

Server-rendered "data islands" bootstrap a responsive client-side app, enabling instant UI updates and complex calculations in the browser.

Key Finding

All financial events are triggered by explicit, user-initiated actions that result in direct service calls. This ensures clarity, control, and a traceable audit trail for every significant financial transaction, from initial material consumption to supplemental cost additions via continuation batches.

I. Architectural Blueprint: The "Hidden" Connections

🎭 The Planning vs. Execution Dichotomy

A Batch in a DRAFT state is a mere plan. It can be edited, changed, or deleted with no financial consequence. The transition to IN_PROGRESS is the "financial sound barrier"—a one-way gate that triggers all valuation and ledger-posting events, after which the core record becomes immutable.

🏝️ The "Data Island" Pattern

The create_batch.html template serves JSON data for templates and stock levels directly into the page. The create_batch_logic.js file reads this data into memory on page load. When a user selects a template, the material list is populated instantly from local JavaScript objects, with no API call required.

🎼 The Orchestrator Service Pattern

The start_batch_production function in batch_service.py is the workflow's epicenter. It doesn't perform the work itself; it directs other specialist services. It commands the costing_service to perform a valuation, then commands the accounting_service to record the transaction.

⚡ Explicit vs. Implicit Triggers

The system uses the right tool for the job. The main, value-creating consumption event is an explicit call (batch_service.start_batch_production) for maximum clarity. Corrective, secondary events (like a ProductionReturn) are handled by implicit Django signals for decoupling and convenience.

II. File & Artifact Manifest

File Path Role in Workflow
inventory/templates/inventory/layout.html Site Shell: Master template providing navigation, CSS/JS assets, and main content block.
inventory/templates/inventory/create_batch.html Entry Point & Data Provider: Renders creation form and delivers critical JSON "data islands" to client.
inventory/templates/inventory/batch_view.html Management Hub: Primary interface for viewing batch state and initiating workflow actions.
static/layout/js/create_batch_logic.js Client-Side Planner: Manages creation form using data islands to dynamically build and validate batch plan.
static/layout/js/batch_view_logic.js Client-Side Controller: Manages detail view, enabling/disabling UI elements based on batch status.
inventory/urls.py Router: Maps all user actions from URLs to correct view functions.
inventory/views/batches.py HTTP Controller: Thin layer that receives web requests and calls appropriate service layer functions.
inventory/services/batch_service.py Orchestrator: The brain of the module, containing business logic for every stage of batch lifecycle.
inventory/services/costing_service.py Valuation Engine: "Time machine" providing historically accurate point-in-time inventory valuation.
inventory/services/accounting/production_transactions.py Ledger Interface: Creates specific, balanced journal entries that post production events to GL.
inventory/models/inventory_management.py Data Schema: Defines core Batch and BatchItem database tables, including circular dependency validation.
inventory/tests_batches.py Verification: Ultimate source of truth, confirming expected behavior and financial outcomes.

III. The End-to-End Workflow Trace

Stage 1: Draft Creation (The Planning Phase)

1. User Action

User navigates to the batch list (batches.html) and clicks "Create New Batch".

2. UI & Client Logic

Page loads. The initCreateBatchLogic JS function parses data islands. User selects a template, and JS reads corresponding items from in-memory templateData object, dynamically building the HTML table. As user adjusts batch count, JS recalculates quantities in real-time.

3. Submission

User submits the form.

4. Backend Processing

create_batch view → batch_service.create_batch: Service validates stock availability and creates DRAFT Batch and BatchItem records.

Outcome: A non-financial plan is stored in the database.

Stage 2: The Approval Workflow

1. Planner Review

Planner views DRAFT batch. Template's conditional logic shows "Submit for Approval" button and keeps form fields editable. Planner submits it.

2. Backend State Change

submit_batch_view: Service changes status to PENDING_APPROVAL.

3. Manager's View

Manager views same page. Template logic now shows "Approve" and "Reject" buttons and adds disabled attribute to form's fieldset, preventing edits. Manager approves the batch.

4. Backend State Change

approve_batch_view: Service changes status to APPROVED.

Outcome: A clear, auditable approval trail is recorded.

Stage 3: Production Start (The Financial Execution) ⚠️

1. User Action

Production manager views APPROVED batch. Template logic shows only "Start Production" button. They click it.

2. Backend Orchestration (The Climax)

start_production_view → batch_service.start_batch_production

Valuation:

costing_service.get_inventory_state_at_datetime is called for each item. It acts as a time machine, querying inventory state at the precise historical moment of batch creation, "burning" cost into BatchItem.cost_at_consumption field.

Accounting:

accounting_service.create_je_for_production_consumption is called. It reads the now-populated cost_at_consumption values and creates immutable JournalEntry: DEBIT Work-in-Progress, CREDIT Raw Materials.

Finalization:

Batch status set to IN_PROGRESS, and Product.moving_average_cost is recalculated for consumed items.

🎉 Outcome: The physical consumption is now a permanent, valued, and balanced transaction in the financial ledger.

IV. The Continuation Batch Workflow (Cost Augmentation)

The Architecturally-Sound Solution

This workflow is the architecturally-sound solution for adding material costs to a production run that is already IN_PROGRESS. It preserves the immutability of the original financial transaction while accurately tracking total production cost.

🔔 Trigger

An IN_PROGRESS parent batch requires more raw materials to complete production.

1. User Action

User creates a new batch with special properties:

  • • Checks the "Is Continuation" checkbox
  • • Selects the parent batch from dropdown
  • • UI automatically populates Shop Order Number and Batch Number range to match parent
  • • User adds only the additional materials required

2. Backend Process (Creation)

A new Batch record is created with is_continuation=True and parent_batch_id pointing to the original. This new batch follows the standard approval workflow (Draft → Pending → Approved).

Note: The continuation batch is a separate, auditable entity with its own approval trail.

3. Financial Event (Execution)

The "Start Production" button is clicked for the continuation batch. This creates a new, separate journal entry for the value of the additional materials:

DEBIT: Work-in-Progress (Additional Material Cost)
CREDIT: Raw Materials Inventory (Additional Material Cost)
Preservation of Immutability: The original parent batch's journal entry remains untouched and unchanged.

4. Cost Aggregation & Finished Goods Receipt

Finished goods are always received against the parent batch. Before this is allowed, a critical validation occurs:

Critical Validation:

finished_product_service ensures that all continuation batches are in IN_PROGRESS or a later state before allowing finished goods receipt. This prevents partial cost calculations.

📊 Total Cost Calculation:

When a FinishedProductReceipt is created, its total_cost is calculated by summing the consumption costs from:

  • ✓ The parent batch
  • ✓ All IN_PROGRESS continuation batches
🎯 Ultimate Outcome

The total production cost is accurately captured across multiple, auditable transactions, all consolidated into the final value of the finished product. Each transaction remains immutable, creating a perfect audit trail.

V. Analysis of Collateral & Corrective Workflows

The module's robustness is further demonstrated by its handling of exceptions and corrections:

Cancelling a Batch

  • • Before Production: Simply marked as CANCELLED with no financial impact.
  • • After IN_PROGRESS: batch_service.cancel_batch creates a full reversing journal entry to perfectly nullify the financial impact.

Adding a Supplemental Item (DEPRECATED)

This workflow has been deprecated in favor of the more robust Continuation Batch method. The system now correctly prevents adding items to a batch that is IN_PROGRESS, guiding the user to the proper procedure.

Migration Path: Users are directed to create a continuation batch instead.

Returning an Item from Production

Creates a ProductionReturn record. A post_save signal on this other model triggers creation of a journal entry to move value back from WIP to Raw Materials, demonstrating a decoupled, event-driven approach for corrective actions.

Preventing Circular Dependencies

Validation has been added to the Batch.clean() method and the batch_service to prevent a user from creating a circular parent-child relationship (e.g., Batch A is parent of B, and B is parent of A), which would otherwise cause a fatal recursion error.

Protection Mechanism: Django validation prevents form submission; service layer validation provides backend safety.
